For palette transformations, infer the complete mapping of every present color—including background, marker, and output colors—from the demos; do not assume foreground identity or reuse a mapping from a previous task. Test the candidate mapping on every cell of every demo before accepting it. If multiple demos show a rectangular frame with missing edge cells recolored, test the foreground bounding box's perimeter as the candidate rule: recolor only background cells on its min/max row or column, never the interior, and accept it only if it exactly reproduces every demo.

Revisit every demo, and run the current transform on each exact demo input; compare the program-produced grids cell-for-cell with the expected outputs before using its test output again. After every edit, rerun all demo regressions. If the demos do not establish the rule (including when the cap is exhausted), keep uncertainty explicit and don't call a heuristic verified. Do not hand-transcribe a grid for submission: a transcription mistake can make a valid ARC answer malformed. If validation fails, fix the input/output serialization and rerun the program; if no transform reproduces every available demo, leave the task file unchanged.
